prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Memory from EARLIER parts of the document (do not extract facts from it; use it only to resolve names, aliases and who produces an item):
Offshore wind O&M; scope Grid Interface Relay (Wildmere); excludes public grid, port ops. Wildmere: Export Limit Advisory→Grid Dispatcher when capability<target; applies accepted ceiling and configured Grid Constraint response; advises Grid Dispatcher of capability changes; keeps protection settings unless authorized switching plan. Grid Dispatcher: requirements→Wildmere. Priority: safety>protection>export; safety over production/maintenance/schedule in all degraded modes. Turbine Controller (Glassfin): validated commands, blocks conflicts, local protective control on supervisory loss, safe mode on auxiliary loss, shutdown on confirmed fire; Pitch Deviation Notice. Pitch System, Rotor Brake Unit, Converter Cabinet (isolated on fire/overheat), Nacelle Condition Monitor→Turbine Sensor Bus. Mode Turbine Lockout: safety-critical fault until assessed and work authorized; no remote restart during fire investigation. Offshore Substation (Morrowick): Main Transformer, export cable, Export Cable Monitor, station service transformers, Fire Detection Panel; Transformer Tap Snapshot→Shore Control Room; Switching Window Acknowledgment; mode Substation Degraded on protection/auxiliary/monitoring impairment. Substation Operator switches only in active window with Control Engineer authorization, notifies Grid Dispatcher. Marine Coordinator, Electrical Technician, Work Permit Portal, Duty Planner support outages. Emergency Generator (Foxglove): auto-start on auxiliary loss, no unapproved paralleling; Start Test Trace; it and Fire Detection Panel essential, never bypassed. SCADA Gateway (Juniper Vale): telemetry/alarms→Shore Control Room (Amber Quay); Session Revocation Receipt→Cybersecurity Gateway; preserves status when degraded; SCADA Engineer investigates. Shore Control Room keeps last validated limit on comms loss. Operations Radio Console: voice to CTV, SOV, Daughter Craft; Vessel Master read-back; Transfer Manifest Addendum from Duty Planner. Personnel Tracking Console; HSE Officer advises re-entry, reviews workarounds; Field Supervisor. North/South Access Scanners deny unauthorized, no override. East/West Service Lifts: interlocks never bypassed. Modes: Weather Hold (Weather Service, Weather Analyst); Vessel Standby (Marine Coordinator, Vessel Master). Degraded: record function, condition, time; escalate beyond envelope; Control Engineer suspends unconfirmed remote commands; Fleet Dispatch Console restrictions→Duty Planner; Maintenance Planning Engine separates safety-critical work. Recovery: condition corrected, equipment stable, inspections before automatic control; Control Engineer coordinates before lifting restrictions.

Document units:
S954: The SCADA Engineer verifies that status, alarms, and command feedback are consistent across the available control views.
S955: The Duty Planner updates operating priorities and deferred work after the recovery status is confirmed.
S956: Normal service is restored in stages so that a successful response at one level does not conceal a remaining restriction elsewhere.
S957: The system retains the event record and recovery decisions for review, trend analysis, and improvement of operating procedures.
S958: The operating concept is governed as a controlled baseline for safe, reliable, and compliant offshore wind farm operations.
S959: The asset operator assigns an accountable owner to maintain the document and coordinate its approval.
S960: Changes to operating assumptions, responsibilities, interfaces, or decision authority require documented impact assessment before approval.
S961: The assessment considers effects on personnel safety, marine coordination, electrical safety, availability, cybersecurity, and regulatory obligations.
S962: The approved concept is consistent with applicable permits, grid requirements, safety cases, and company management systems.
S963: The Shore Control Room applies the approved operating concept during routine operations and abnormal conditions.
S964: The Control Engineer reviews control-room practices and confirms that operational procedures remain consistent with the concept.
S965: The Duty Planner checks that maintenance priorities, resource plans, and operational constraints are reflected in planned work.
S966: The Marine Coordinator reviews vessel coordination arrangements and verifies that marine responsibilities are understood.
S967: The HSE Officer evaluates safety controls, emergency arrangements, and lessons from reported events.
S968: The SCADA Engineer reviews monitoring and control assumptions that affect operational decisions.
S969: The Cybersecurity Analyst assesses changes that could affect access, communications, or the integrity of operational records.
S970: The Field Supervisor confirms that field execution practices and escalation routes are workable for offshore personnel.
S971: The Substation Operator reviews responsibilities and coordination arrangements for substation activities.
S972: Assurance evidence includes approved procedures, competence records, maintenance records, risk assessments, audit findings, and event investigations.
S973: Evidence is retained in controlled repositories with access permissions, revision history, and defined retention periods.
S974: Reviews distinguish verified evidence from assumptions, unresolved actions, and proposals that have not yet been approved.
S975: Nonconformances and operational lessons are assigned to an accountable owner with a due date and closure evidence.
S976: The document owner schedules periodic review and initiates an additional review after material operational, technical, or regulatory change.
